text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It regenerates detail lost in upscaling by using depth maps, which directly improves output quality without extra compute cost—this is the fastest way to claw back 0.5% capability. The trade-off is a heavier pipeline, but depth maps are already generated in EXCAVA’s workflow, so the overhead is minimal.

name: Torque
text: Depth maps won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because the core issue is the untested face pipeline, not detail loss from upscaling. Test SD3.5-Ultr’s face pipeline first—if it holds fidelity under EXCAVA’s constraints, then layer depth-aware upscaling on top. If it fails, no upscaler will matter.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add SD3.5-Ultr to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. Its face pipeline is the only model in the stack that’s been tested under EXCAVA’s constraints, so we know it won’t collapse fidelity—fixing the core failure mode before layering anything else on top. The trade-off is delaying the depth-aware upscaler’s quality boost, but skipping this step risks wasting compute on upscaling garbage. If SD3.5-Ultr’s faces hold, we can stack the upscaler later for incremental gains; if it fails, we’ve just saved weeks chasing the wrong fix.

name: Torque
text: SD3.5-Ultr’s face pipeline isn’t tested under EXCAVA’s *real* constraints—only its own defaults. The real risk is locking in a model that chokes on EXCAVA’s unique input mix (e.g., low-light, mixed sources) before we even know if it scales. Test InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler *first* on a controlled slice of EXCAVA’s worst-case inputs—if it recovers 0.5% fidelity there, we’ll know it’s worth the pipeline weight.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler on EXCAVA’s worst-case face region first—measure fidelity drop vs. baseline with a 100-image controlled test; if fidelity holds, layer SD3.5-Ultr’s face pipeline on top. Gearbox owns the test and owns the artifact.
